recipes.title: Croissants · direct dough
recipes.description: Michel Suas · croissants · printed pp.331. Source discrepancy / calculated adaptation disclosed.

stages.name: Détrempe additions + separate roll-in butter · p.331

rows.name: Roll-in butter · lamination only, not mixer butter

methods.heading: Before mixing
methods.body: Keep dough butter and roll-in butter separate. Only the dough butter goes into the mixer; reserve the roll-in butter for lamination. The 25% roll-in percentage uses détrempe weight, not flour weight. Finished batch weight includes lamination butter once. (Suas, p.311; pp.331.)

methods.heading: Mix
methods.body: Use an improved mix for the détrempe. Hold sugar back until gluten development when it exceeds 10% of flour, then incorporate it. Target dough temperature 22–25°C.  (Suas, p.312; pp.331.)

methods.heading: First fermentation
methods.body: Ferment 45–60 minutes, then refrigerate 8–15 hours at 4°C. Enter the cold hold separately in the planner. (Suas, pp.331.)

methods.heading: Prepare lamination butter
methods.body: Use cold butter that is firm but pliable, with texture and temperature compatible with the chilled dough. Pound between heavy plastic sheets to form an even block; do not melt or spread warm butter. Enclose it in the dough before giving the turns. (Suas, pp.311–313.)

methods.heading: Laminate
methods.body: Give three single (letter) folds. Sheet gradually and evenly, fold in thirds, and rotate 90° between turns. Rest 30 minutes in the refrigerator between folds or series of folds. After the last fold, refrigerate at least 30 minutes before final sheeting. Plan all turns, handling and rests in the lamination field; do not count these rests again as bench time. (Suas, pp.315,317; pp.331.)

methods.heading: Shape
methods.body: Sheet the rested dough to 3–3.5 mm and allow it to relax before cutting. For traditional croissants, cut a 41 cm wide sheet into two 20.5 cm strips, then triangles with 10.25 cm bases. Gently stretch, roll from base toward tip without damaging the shoulders, and pan on parchment with room to expand. Apply a thin egg wash after shaping; it is an unquantified finishing ingredient, not part of dough mass. (Suas, pp.317–318.)

methods.heading: Final proof
methods.body: Proof 1½–2 hours at 26°C and 65% relative humidity. Check the dough’s readiness rather than treating the clock as proof of readiness. Apply a gentle thin egg wash again before baking, avoiding pooled wash and glued layers. (Suas, p.317; pp.331.)

methods.heading: Bake
methods.body: Bake in a convection oven for 13–15 minutes at 196°C (385°F), with 2 seconds of steam. The planner’s finish is oven exit and excludes cooling. (Suas, pp.331.)

notes: Printed metric kilogram quantities are converted to grams. Original local-table percentages are preserved; they are not whole-batch percentages. Butter for roll-in is 25% of détrempe, not a flour-based baker’s percentage; its source percentage cell is therefore intentionally blank.

The batch includes roll-in butter, but it must not be mixed into the détrempe. Base piece count 48 is an editable planning assumption, not a yield stated in Suas. Egg wash and dusting flour are unquantified finishing aids and are not included in the mass.

The flour/water calculation counts only explicit water and flour, tracing only consumed build fractions. Milk, eggs and butter contain unquantified water; seed hydration is not guessed. Do not treat the displayed direct-water ratio as full effective hydration.

Planner: enter cold holding and all lamination work/rests in the dedicated required fields. Enter 0 for unused warm bulk or bench stages. Prefermented-dough build time includes its unspecified cold hold. Natural-starter builds are sequential, not parallel.
warnings: Suas p.331 prints 385°F (96°C). Calculated conversion: (385−32)×5/9 = 196.1°C; the working bake uses 196°C, also printed for the other croissant formulas. The original 96°C is retained here as a source discrepancy.

methods.heading: Prepare prefermented dough
methods.body: Combine the build ingredients; DDT 21°C. Ferment 1 hour at 18–21°C, then refrigerate until needed. The cold duration is not specified; include your chosen hold in the build timing. (Suas, p.345.)

methods.heading: Before mixing
methods.body: Keep dough butter and roll-in butter separate. Only the dough butter goes into the mixer; reserve the roll-in butter for lamination. The 25% roll-in percentage uses détrempe weight, not flour weight. Finished batch weight includes lamination butter once. (Suas, p.311; pp.345–346.)

methods.heading: Mix
methods.body: Use an improved mix for the détrempe. Hold sugar back until gluten development when it exceeds 10% of flour, then incorporate it. Target dough temperature 22–25°C.  (Suas, p.312; pp.345–346.)

methods.heading: First fermentation
methods.body: Ferment 45–60 minutes, then refrigerate 1 hour at 5°C. Enter the cold hold separately in the planner. (Suas, pp.345–346.)

methods.heading: Prepare lamination butter
methods.body: Use cold butter that is firm but pliable, with texture and temperature compatible with the chilled dough. Pound between heavy plastic sheets to form an even block; do not melt or spread warm butter. Enclose it in the dough before giving the turns. (Suas, pp.311–313.)

methods.heading: Laminate
methods.body: Give three single (letter) folds. Sheet gradually and evenly, fold in thirds, and rotate 90° between turns. Rest 30 minutes in the refrigerator between folds or series of folds. After the last fold, refrigerate at least 30 minutes before final sheeting. Plan all turns, handling and rests in the lamination field; do not count these rests again as bench time. (Suas, pp.315,317; pp.345–346.)

methods.heading: Shape
methods.body: Sheet the rested dough to 3–3.5 mm and allow it to relax before cutting. For traditional croissants, cut a 41 cm wide sheet into two 20.5 cm strips, then triangles with 10.25 cm bases. Gently stretch, roll from base toward tip without damaging the shoulders, and pan on parchment with room to expand. Apply a thin egg wash after shaping; it is an unquantified finishing ingredient, not part of dough mass. (Suas, pp.317–318.)

methods.heading: Final proof
methods.body: Proof 1½–2 hours at 26°C and 65% relative humidity. Check the dough’s readiness rather than treating the clock as proof of readiness. Apply a gentle thin egg wash again before baking, avoiding pooled wash and glued layers. (Suas, p.317; pp.345–346.)

methods.heading: Bake
methods.body: Bake in a convection oven for 13–15 minutes at 196°C (385°F), with 2 seconds of steam. The planner’s finish is oven exit and excludes cooling. (Suas, pp.345–346.)
